newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president orders cutting government jobs.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president orders cutting government jobs.

text.p: President Kim Young-sam, campaigning to improve the South Korean economy's competitiveness, on Thursday ordered cutting 10,000 government jobs and a streamlining of the bureaucracy, his spokesman said.
Kim told his cabinet ministers to work out measures to improve the country's competitiveness by 10 percent to end the problem of the economy saddled with high costs and low efficiency.
"The government and the public sector should set an example to promote cooperation from the people for achieving the national task," Kim was quoted as sying.
"For this purpose, the public sector should save more than one trillion won ($1.18 billion) in its budget and reduce 10,000 government employees...to remove inefficiency," he was quoted as saying.
No timetable was given for the layoffs, which would represent a reduction of one percent of the government workforce.
The order to cut government jobs comes as Kim is pushing through labour reform via controversial new labour legislation.
Industrial action has flared in South Korea since Kim's ruling party rammed a new labour bill through parliament on December 26 in a six-minute session in the absence of opposition deputies.
The new law ends decades of near-total job security by allowing employers to lay off workers and hire temporary workers to replace strikers.
The spokesman said Kim also ordered the cabinet to streamline restrictions in various sectors.
